utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-42/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We're here for a Status Conference in the case against Mr. Kovacevic. Although one could argue if an accused who is on provisional release, whether a Status Conference should be held, similarly as provided for in the Rules, there were reasons to at least call a Status Conference at this moment. May I have the appearances. Prosecution, first. Ms. Somers, I take it you're accompanied by?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I am accompanied by the same persons who were here earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's another --.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I will introduce them again. Our case manager has not made it in, but let me just continue. Susan Somers for the Prosecution. To my right, Mr. David Re. Behind me, Mr. Aleksandar Kontic and Phillip Weiner. And when our manager enters, it will be Ms. Carmela Javier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. For the Defence, Tanja Radosavljevic as the counsel, assisted by Mr. Dragoslav Djukic as the case manager. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We have invited representatives of Serbia to be present. Could they present themselves. Mr. Obradovic, these are different proceedings. That's the reason why we have to put everything on record again and again. So you are invited to introduce yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It is a pleasure anyway. My name is Sasa Obradovic. I'm the First Councillor of the Embassy of Serbia in The Hague, and today with me on behalf of the Serbian government is the Deputy Prosecutor for War Crimes, Mr. Dusan Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obradovic. Usually at Status Conferences, issues like disclosure, et cetera, are on the agenda. We have an open agenda today. There's one issue that the Chamber would like to hear more about. That is the issue of reports about Mr. Kovacevic, who has been provisionally released, and related to that, any observations by Serbia in respect of concerns that have been expressed by the Defence on the conditions in psychiatric institutions. Just to cut it short, Serbia has asked permission to move Mr. Kovacevic from the hospital where he is at present to another hospital. The request seemed to be an urgent one and was related to the medical condition of Mr. Kovacevic. The Chamber quickly responded to that request. Then Ms. Radosavljevic expressed in writing concerns about the conditions in the hospital to which Mr. Kovacevic would be transferred. Since the transfer had not been that urgent, that it had already taken place, the Chamber, on the basis of the concerns, had suspended its permission, and since then no further information reached the Chamber. If I might put this first on the agenda, and then ask later if there's anything else that the parties would like to raise, then I would like to give an opportunity to Ms. Radosavljevic to inform me on whether any further information reached her, apart from the information that has already been brought to the attention of the Chamber, and whether she would like to further elaborate on it. Ms. Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Since my reply to the request of the state, I haven't received any further information on this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So matters stand as they were, I think it was, early August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, I don't know whether the Prosecution has an opinion about the matter or whether it leaves it mainly to the Chamber, the Defence, and the reporting state.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We leave it to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Somers. Then, Mr. Obradovic, may I invite you to, first of all, respond to the concerns expressed by Ms. Radosavljevic. You are aware of the concerns expressed. And could I, once you've done that, invite you also to inform me, and by that, the Chamber, why reporting had not taken place within the time limits set in the order for provisional release? Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in view of the complexity and sensitivity of the matter, I will do my best to stay within the bounds of what is reliable information only. And it is with absolute reliability that I can inform Your Honour of the following: The fact of the matter is that the physicians and the medical staff of the psychiatric clinic of the Military Medical Academy in Belgrade did come across certain difficulties in providing security for his patient, who is the accused in this case, Vladimir Kovacevic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. If it would be necessary, or if you would like to go into details which are not suitable for a public hearing because they directly are linked to medical issues concerning Mr. Kovacevic which are not suitable for a public hearing, then please address me and ask me whether we go into private session. Then you'll feel perhaps more free to speak and the Chamber gets better information and the interests of Mr. Kovacevic will then be properly protected. So whenever there's any need, don't hesitate to address me. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for the suggestion. In that case, I would ask you, to be on the safe side, to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For those following the proceedings here, we have stayed a little too long in private session. The representative of Serbia has told me that he has two reports, one report dated the 6th of September about the treatment of Mr. Kovacevic, a report by Dr. Radovanovic, and another report also of the 6th of September in which the competence of Mr. Kovacevic to stand trial is dealt with, a report which is drafted by three physicians. The parties will now receive copies of those reports for brief inspection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to invite Ms. Radosavljevic to inform me about the content of the report, so not to interpret it in any way but just to inform me about what it says. And then, Ms. Somers, I take it that you'll be able to form your opinion on whether that's information similar to what you received. Ms. Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The first letter, the report on the medical state of Mr. Vladimir Kovacevic, signed by the Chief of the Psychiatry, Dr. Miroslav Radovanovic, and maybe this would be a good moment to re-enter private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll turn into private session. [Private session].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Open session].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Radosavljevic, is there any comment you'd like to make or any matter to be raised in relation to this report?

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In relation to the documents that we received, no, I don't have any comments right now. I am just wondering, we spoke at the Rule 11 bis hearing on the possibility of presenting to the Referral Chamber the documents that we spoke about. In legal terms, I agree with what my learned friend uttered, in terms who is authorised to give a legal finding. I would just like to say that, in my opinion, these two papers should be given also to the Referral Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What's your opinion on that, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm not sure of the value of it, because if the finding by -- the relevant finding is the finding by Your Honour, and of course the Prosecution's position is that that particular finding is not relevant to referral. So we would find no value evidentiarially or even a reason for further reporting unless the Bench were minded to hold another hearing. I assume this wouldn't be at this stage, and particularly in light of the comments that should there be a referral, there would be an immediate evaluation in a foreign country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have now learned about the content of these reports. These reports, I would say, do not or are not such that they would undermine the decision given by the Trial Chamber. I mean, it does not contradict -- whatever the value may be, whether it's sound or not, but certainly these reports would not contradict the finding of the Trial Chamber. At the same time, the first report about the present medical status reflects a deterioration of the medical situation of the patient. I don't think that the Referral Bench would go into any details as far as medical matters are concerned. This is very global information. If you could agree that this information would, for the time being and for the purposes of the Referral Bench, be sufficient, then it is on the public record now and the Referral Bench, of course in a transparent way, could express that it has knowledge of this summary of what these reports tell us. I'm trying to avoid that we get a whole new round of litigation on something which is really marginal at this moment. I mean, Mr. Kovacevic is a psychiatric patient, is a serious psychiatric patient, and whether he is a little bit more serious psychiatric patient is, of course, something we should not spend ages on. Ms. Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to state that I disagree with my learned friend that these two papers have no relevance for the Rule 11 bis hearing that we had today, because -- and I'm now talking about just the first document, not the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Because this actually supports the submission of the Defence that was uttered in a private session. So, therefore, I think they are relevant for the Referral Bench, of course to value them as they see fit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least one could say that what you said in private session at the time, you expressed some concern about new examinations that might have their influence, that at least the present status does not make that argument any less valid than it was without this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we just see that as having no real value other than perhaps there is a requirement of periodic medical reports. So the first report, perhaps. But the attempt at opinions on issues that are not in the competence that are in the second report, we think, should not be factored in at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Could the parties agree that the first report, as reflecting the present status of Mr. Kovacevic, would be brought to the attention of the Referral Bench? And leave the second. We have not asked for the second one, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: We would. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: The Defence agrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that has been settled. Then, Ms. Radosavljevic, I do understand that at this moment the transfer of Mr. Kovacevic to another clinic is not -- not only not urgent, but it's not an issue at this moment, although it's not entirely clear to me whether it was that the Lazar Lazarevic clinic could not provide the treatment or could not provide the necessary security. I do understand that it's not at this moment something under consideration. In view of this, would you like, nevertheless, to respond to what has been said by Mr. Obradovic, or -- I'm not keeping you from doing it, but I'm also looking at the clock and ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not at the time being. The Defence has uttered in its submission the point of view in regards to the clinic that we are talking about, Lazar Lazarevic. And, as the representative of the state informed the Trial Chamber, the state received also information from that specific clinic that they do not have the capacity or the conditions for Mr. Kovacevic to be treated there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So whatever may have been the situation at the clinic, it's not relevant for Mr. Kovacevic at this moment. Yes. Then, is there any other matter the parties would like to raise? Ms. Radosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe it's too early to pose this question, but the Defence submitted a request for certification in regards to a decision of the Trial Chamber of the dismissal of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. And you'll receive a decision on that request. Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Nothing further, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing further? Any further need to address the Chamber, Mr. Obradovic? I see you nodding no. Then we'll stand adjourned sine die.
